name: IEC random-access memory (RAM)
summary: IEC element marked RAM with address grouping, a write control input and A-labelled data inputs and outputs.
description: A RAM symbol carries the RAM qualifier and organisation. Address inputs form an A group; a write input is labelled with control dependency, and data inputs are labelled A plus the control number and D, meaning data is written to the addressed word when the control is active. Data outputs are labelled A.
TI's overview builds a 16-word by 4-bit memory from latches to explain this notation. On drawings, RAM symbols document buffers in communication modules and processor boards.
The symbol does not state whether the memory is static or dynamic, its retention behaviour, or any battery backup. Note those where data must survive power loss.
readingNotes: Write control appears as a C input; data inputs carry A and the control number.
drawingChecklist: Show write and enable controls with dependency labels.
distinction: ROM has no write inputs; FIFO memory has no address inputs.
